study.sourceLabel: BIS/11/803, WERS6 Management Questionnaire (MQ), Section C and the EPQ items it depends on (GOV.UK)
study.abstract: This study contains Section C (recruitment, training and organisation of work) of the management interview of the sixth Workplace Employment Relations Study (WERS 2011), a CAPI interview with the most senior manager responsible for staff and employment relations at British workplaces, plus the employee-profile items it builds on (number of employees, occupational structure). The manager reports how vacancies are filled and which recruitment criteria, tests and channels are used, and, for the largest non-managerial occupational group, induction, the share given off-the-job training, training days and training content, multi-skilling, job autonomy and teamworking. A last item asks for the share of all employees using computers.
study.universe: Workplaces in Great Britain with at least 5 employees; respondent: the most senior manager responsible for staff and employment relations at the workplace. Most of Section C refers to the largest non-managerial occupational group of the workplace.

survey.name: zsocdesc
survey.label:
From what you have said, the largest non-managerial group of employees at this workplace is classified as [LOGIDX: TITLE OF LARGEST OCCUPATIONAL GROUP].
How would you describe the main tasks and activities of this largest group?
survey.guidance_hint: INTERVIEWER: Probe for details about the most common job in this group, record verbatim: OPEN

survey.name: section_c
survey.label: RECRUITMENT, TRAINING AND ORGANISATION OF WORK

survey.name: cfillvac
survey.label: Which of these statements best describes your approach to filling vacancies at this workplace?
survey.guidance_hint:
SHOW CARD C1
INTERVIEWER: For larger public sector employers, individual departments and agencies should be treated as separate employers

survey.name: cfactors
survey.label: Which of the following factors are important when recruiting new employees?
survey.guidance_hint:
SHOW CARD C2
PROBE: Which others? UNTIL 'None'.
CODE ALL THAT APPLY.

survey.name: cfactors_other
survey.label: Other (please specify CFACTOTH)

survey.name: cspecix
survey.label: When filling vacancies, do you have any special procedures to encourage applications from the following groups?
survey.guidance_hint:
SHOW CARD C3
PROBE: Which others? UNTIL 'None'.
CODE ALL THAT APPLY.

survey.name: catestw
survey.label: When filling vacancies at this workplace, do you ever conduct any type of personality or attitude test for managerial positions, non-managerial positions or not at all?
survey.guidance_hint: CODE ALL THAT APPLY.

survey.name: cptestw
survey.label: When filling vacancies at this workplace, do you ever conduct any type of performance or competency test for managerial positions, non-managerial positions or not at all?
survey.guidance_hint: CODE ALL THAT APPLY.

survey.name: clogvac
survey.label:
Now I would like to ask you about the largest non-managerial group of employees here, that is, the [LOGIDX: TITLE OF THE LARGEST OCCUPATIONAL GROUP].
Have there been any vacancies for [LOGIDX: TITLE OF THE LARGEST OCCUPATIONAL GROUP] in the past 12 months?

survey.name: cchanx
survey.label: This card shows a list of recruitment channels. What are the three most common channels used when trying to fill these vacancies?
survey.guidance_hint:
SHOW CARD C4
PROBE: Which others? UNTIL 'None'.

survey.name: cchanx_other
survey.label: Some other way (please specify COTHCHN)

survey.name: cinduct
survey.label: Is there a standard induction programme designed to introduce new [LOGIDX: TITLE OF THE LARGEST OCCUPATIONAL GROUP] to this workplace?
survey.guidance_hint: INTERVIEWER: Do not include probation periods.

survey.name: cstuckin
survey.label: About how long does it normally take before new [LOGIDX: TITLE OF THE LARGEST OCCUPATIONAL GROUP] are able to do their job as well as more experienced employees already working here?
survey.guidance_hint: SHOW CARD C5

survey.name: trintro
survey.label: I am now going to ask about training activities. I am interested in all training for which employees are given a break from their normal work duties, whether the training takes place at their immediate work position or elsewhere.

survey.name: coffjob
survey.label: What proportion of experienced [LOGIDX: TITLE OF THE LARGEST OCCUPATIONAL GROUP] have been given time off from their normal daily work duties to undertake training over the past 12 months?
survey.guidance_hint: SHOW CARD C6

survey.name: coffchk
survey.label: Did any experienced [LOGIDX: TITLE OF THE LARGEST OCCUPATIONAL GROUP] have time off from their normal daily work duties to undertake training over the past 12 months?

survey.name: ctrain
survey.label: On average, how many days of training did experienced [LOGIDX: TITLE OF THE LARGEST OCCUPATIONAL GROUP] undertake over the past 12 months?

survey.name: chow
survey.label: Did this training cover any of the matters listed on this card?:
survey.guidance_hint:
SHOW CARD C7
PROBE: Which others? UNTIL 'None'.
CODE ALL THAT APPLY.

survey.name: cothjob
survey.label: Approximately, what proportion of [LOGIDX: TITLE OF THE LARGEST OCCUPATIONAL GROUP] are formally trained to be able to do jobs other than their own?
survey.guidance_hint:
SHOW CARD C8
INTERVIEWER: If respondent gives answer as an exact number you can code “97” here and record the number at the next question.

survey.name: cothjobt
survey.label: (How many [LOGIDX: TITLE OF THE LARGEST OCCUPATIONAL GROUP] are formally trained to be able to do jobs other than their own?)
survey.guidance_hint:
ENTER NUMBER
SOFT CHECK if COTHJOBT>ZALLEMPS: "Are you sure? The number recorded here is greater than the total number of employees recorded at the start of the interview."

survey.name: cothdo
survey.label: And approximately, what proportion of [LOGIDX: TITLE OF THE LARGEST OCCUPATIONAL GROUP] actually do jobs other than their own at least once a week?
survey.guidance_hint:
SHOW CARD C8
INTERVIEWER: If respondent gives answer as an exact number you can code “97” here and record the number at the next question.

survey.name: cothdot
survey.label: (And approximately, how many [LOGIDX: TITLE OF THE LARGEST OCCUPATIONAL GROUP] actually do jobs other than their own at least once a week?)
survey.guidance_hint:
ENTER NUMBER
SOFT CHECK if COTHDOT>ZALLEMPS: "Are you sure? The number recorded here is greater than the total number of employees recorded at the start of the interview."

survey.name: cvariety
survey.label: ...variety in their work?
survey.guidance_hint: SHOW CARD C9

survey.name: cdiscrete
survey.label: ...discretion over how they do their work? :
survey.guidance_hint: SHOW CARD C9

survey.name: control
survey.label: ...control over the pace at which they work? :
survey.guidance_hint: SHOW CARD C9

survey.name: cdesign
survey.label: ...involvement in decisions over how their work is organised?
survey.guidance_hint: SHOW CARD C9

survey.name: cteams
survey.label: What proportion, if any, of [LOGIDX: TITLE OF THE LARGEST OCCUPATIONAL GROUP] at this workplace work in formally designated teams?
survey.guidance_hint:
SHOW CARD C10
INTERVIEWER: If respondent gives answer as an exact number you can code “97” here and record the number at the next question

survey.name: cteamst
survey.label: (How many [LOGIDX: TITLE OF THE LARGEST OCCUPATIONAL GROUP] at this workplace work in formally designated teams?)
survey.guidance_hint:
ENTER NUMBER
SOFT CHECK if CTEAMST>ZALLEMPS: "Are you sure? The number recorded here is greater than the total number of employees recorded at the start of the interview."

survey.name: cteamho
survey.label: Do each of the following statements apply to the way that teamworking operates among [LOGIDX: TITLE OF THE LARGEST OCCUPATIONAL GROUP] at this workplace?

survey.name: cteamhoa
survey.label: ...Team members depend on each other's work to be able to do their job.

survey.name: cteamhoc
survey.label: ...Team members jointly decide how the work is to be done.

survey.name: cteamhod
survey.label: ...Teams are given responsibility for specific products or services.

survey.name: ccomput
survey.label:
I would now like you to think about the whole workforce at this workplace.
In this workplace, what percentage of all employees use computers as part of their normal work duties? Please answer to the nearest 10%.
survey.guidance_hint:
INTERVIEWER: If respondent gives answer as an exact number you can code “997” here and record the number at the next question.
SOFT CHECK if CCOMPUT>100 and CCOMPUT≠997: "The number entered here is a percentage. It should not be greater than 100."

survey.name: ccomputt
survey.label: (In this workplace, how many employees use computers as part of their normal work duties?)
survey.guidance_hint:
ENTER NUMBER
SOFT CHECK if CCOMPUTT>ZALLEMPS: "Are you sure? The number recorded here is greater than the total number of employees recorded at the start of the interview."
